q: How much CO2 does using more cullet save in a glass furnace?
title: Cullet in a glass furnace: CO2 saved
short: Cullet saves in two ways. It replaces soda ash and limestone, so their process CO2 is never released. It also melts with less energy, so furnace fuel falls. Measure both: carbonates charged and fuel per tonne of glass, before and after.

ul: Tonnes of cullet, soda ash and limestone charged.
Furnace fuel per tonne of glass pulled.
Bought cullet, with the supplier's invoices.

p: Soda ash releases 0.415 t CO2 per tonne and limestone 0.440 t CO2 per tonne. Less of each in the batch means less process CO2.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
